filter_5_definition_as_read.ribbon_definition: backtest/lib/ribbon.py -- Saty Pivot Ribbon, EMA fast=13 / pivot=20 / slow=48 on 5-min SPY closes. stack='BULL' iff fast>pivot>slow STRICTLY; 'BEAR' iff fast<pivot<slow STRICTLY; otherwise 'MIXED'. So filter 5 demands a STRICT 3-EMA ordering at the trigger bar, on the same side as the trade.

The only scorecard that measures filter-5-blocked setups at all is structure-shift-cascade-ab-2026-07-28.json -- and that tests a RELAXATION of filter 5, presupposing the gate. It never validated the gate itself.
provenance_finding_stated_before_measure.consequence: Under J's standing rule (memory: kill_reentry_lock_gate_provenance_2026_07_02 -- 'every gate needs provenance + evidence or it dies'), filter 5 currently has neither. It survives only if THIS study's measurement earns it.

hypothesis: H1: Filter 5 is a lagging veto whose block-set is NOT net-negative. Specifically: the cohort of setups it blocks while every OTHER blocker is empty (blockers == [5] exactly) has POSITIVE real-OPRA expectancy when walked through the real exit manager, and removing/scoping the gate improves the book -- most importantly over the RECENT window, because a gate positive over 390 days but negative over 25 is a DEAD gate (J 2026-07-31: 'the same thing that worked on day 372 ago is not gonna work on day 162 ago').
